decision: A once-loaded ring changes the bond distance between the same two old shared marks. A three-step pair reads 13/15 quiet/loaded at layers one through three and 13/12 at layer four. The adjacent marks stay 7/4 from layer four. Ordinary step lengths stay fixed. First-layer straddling changes stay two on arbitrarily long paths.
evidence: Exact computation and proofs within the documented law, preparations, and event conventions
sample: One per original physical pair, one per physical shortest route for that pair, one per distinct knot in a ball and one per allowed assignment on the fixed dose comparison.

measured_objects.object: bond distance between fixed original distinctions after one ring load
measured_objects.standard: literal minimal nonfree support size minus one
measured_objects.population: 210 original pairs in both one-spare arms at ages one and two, plus both rings at two spacings and named later pairs
measured_objects.definition: minimum connected-shore cost for the two marked shared distinctions less one
measured_objects.outcome: 75 larger and 135 equal through two layers, then an opposite sign on the same pair at layer four

measured_objects.object: persistent bond distance for the two background marks meeting the ring
measured_objects.standard: exact upper and lower bond witnesses
measured_objects.population: either ring on the single and two-ring controls in every finite layer
measured_objects.definition: two marked shared distinctions on the attachment's two original path neighbors
measured_objects.outcome: 7 quiet at every size, 7 loaded through age three and 4 at every later size

measured_objects.object: length and multiplicity of shortest routes between old shared marks under feedback
measured_objects.population: 120 fixed pairs in 174 reached physical stages plus the last quiet-double route from the funded roster
measured_objects.definition: two incidence hops per mark step; count every shortest forward physical route
measured_objects.outcome: all lengths fixed at every size; 44 crossing pairs lose routes under one-ring loading; outermost stable counts 3432 and 2220

measured_objects.object: knot counts around all midpoints of old-pair shortest routes
measured_objects.standard: each knot counts once through its first saturation radius
measured_objects.population: all 20,880 physical pair-stage profiles and fixed-source midpoint controls
measured_objects.definition: distance in incidence hops from the nearest shortest-route midpoint
measured_objects.outcome: three-step pair at age two gives 14/16 within two hops, fixed original midpoint 9/9; both give 58/71 within six

validation: Independent algorithms or mathematical lower and upper controls, literal replay, scoped validation, frozen-input checks.
